newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Bekaert shares hit by Dupont tyre.
newsitem.headline: Bekaert shares hit by Dupont tyre.

text.p: Shares in Belgian steel wire and cord maker Bekaert fell sharply on Tuesday after U.S. chemical giant Dupont said it had developed a fibre that replaces steel cord in tyres and reduces their weight.
"The market is definitely overreacting to Dupont's advertisement in the Economist this weekend," Bekaert's vice-president Willy Snaet told Reuters.
Bekaert shares fell over seven percent in early trading but recovered somewhat at 1415 GMT, down 4.61 percent to 23,800 francs, after closing on Monday at 24,950 francs.
Dupont's advertisement said the new tyre would reduce overall weight by 30 percent and in turn cut fuel consumption.
But Snaet said the tyre which uses the fibre, called Kevlar, is 20 percent more expensive than normal tyres, adding that in the short to medium term it was not a threat.
He said Bekaert received a report every two years from the Stanford Research Institute (SRI) on Kevlar development and the latest report concluded it was less of a threat now than 10 years ago.
Bekaert produces steel cord tyre reinforcement and controls 22 percent of the world market, according to an Investext Broker's Report in July.
The new Kevlar tyre, called ULW, produced by Dunlop has been installed on the new Audi A3 cars.
Snaet said the quality of steel cord had increased while the price had fallen. He said that Kevlar tyres were expensive as it was too costly to invest in expansion.
General Bank steel analyst Sandra Vandersmissen agreed.

"To produce Kevlar would not necessarily be economically viable at the moment as one would have to set up new factories because of its completely new technology," she said. "The product looks more promising in the long term".
Dealers said the market was overreacting to the Dupont advertisement and expected the price to recover.
"We are thinking of changing our recommendation to hold from sell," Vandersmissen said.
